scope: A kitchen note for some units with an implied remainder («dos hamburguesas, una sin cebolla», or «una sin cebolla» after ordering two) notes only those units and keeps the rest plain; counted notes («una / las dos sin <ingrediente>») accept any ingredient
trigger: Pending priority from batches 81 and 84 (per-unit notes)
baselineFindings: «dos hamburguesas clasicas, una sin cebolla» added ×2 with «sin cebolla» on both units, agent on and off
«3 hamburguesas clasicas, dos sin tomate» put the note on all three units
After «dos hamburguesas clasicas», «una sin cebolla» noted the whole ×2 line (only «una de las hamburguesas sin cebolla» or an explicit «y la otra normal» split it)
On a one-unit line, «una sin alcaparras» and «las dos sin alcaparras» showed the cart and dropped the note: the counted-note detector only knew a fixed ingredient list (cebolla, ají, sal, tomate…)
fix: parsePartialNote returns an implied split for «(y) M (de ellas) sin/poco/poca/bien/extra …» (no «más/otra/adicional/normal/y …»); tryHandlePartialUnitKitchenNote applies it only to a single unnoted cart line with more units than M and otherwise lets the existing flow continue. The same-SKU text expansion rewrites «N <plato>, (y) M (de ellas) sin/poco/poca …» with M < N ≤ 30 and a single attribute-free product into «(N−M) <plato> y M <plato> <nota>». The kitchen-note detector accepts any ingredient after a counted subject («una / las dos / ambas / todas … sin X»).

contrasts: one-unit line: «una sin X» still notes that line
«las dos sin X» notes both units
explicit «una sin X y la otra normal» still splits
«una sin X y la otra sin Y» in one message gives each unit its note
two different one-unit lines: «una sin X» splits nothing (the existing last-line note is unchanged)
a line that already has a note is not split by an implied note
«dos <plato>, tres sin X» is not split
parser: «una más sin cebolla», «otra sin cebolla», «una sin cebolla adicional», «una sin cebolla y otra sin tomate» are not implied splits
